sentenceSets.sentence: The committee was stupefied by the disclosure, having had no indication that the situation had developed as far as it had.

answerChoices.reasoning: Shocked means surprised and upset; the sentence shows the committee reacting to unexpected information, but stupefied emphasizes being rendered dazed and unclear-thinking, not just emotionally shocked.
Stunned means temporarily dazed; the sentence shows the committee reacting to unexpected information, but stupefied emphasizes being rendered groggy and unclear-minded.
Astonished means greatly surprised; the sentence shows the committee surprised by information, but stupefied emphasizes being rendered mentally dazed and insensible.
Flabbergasted means extremely surprised and confused; the sentence shows the committee surprised by disclosure, but stupefied emphasizes the mental dulling and insensibility.
Surprised means caught off guard; the sentence shows the committee reacting to unexpected information, but stupefied emphasizes the mental dulling effect.
Bewildered means confused and perplexed; the sentence shows confusion by disclosure, but stupefied emphasizes being rendered groggy and insensible.
Confused means unclear in mind; the sentence shows the committee confused by information, but stupefied emphasizes the dazed groggy state.
Dumbfounded means left speechless with surprise; the sentence shows the committee reacting to disclosure, but stupefied emphasizes mental dulling, not speechlessness.
Pleased means satisfied or content; the sentence describes the committee stupefied by unexpected disclosure, implying distress, not pleasure.
Prepared means ready in advance; the sentence emphasizes the committee had no indication of the situation, the opposite of being prepared.
Enlightened means given understanding; the sentence describes the committee stupefied by disclosure, implying mental confusion, not illumination.
